_about: EVERY RING, AND HOW BIG EACH ONE IS.
Every size is a percent of the stream's width at that spot: 100 = as wide as the stream is there.
A ring whose size is not 0 is never thinner than 1 block, so a brook keeps every ring.
Each ring has ONE size, its reach, along one distance: blocks out from the water's edge PLUS blocks up
(or down) from the water surface. The waterline takes everything within its reach, above or below the water;
under the water past that is the bed; the bank rings follow outward, their reaches adding up.
Above the water nothing is painted past a quarter of the stream's width from the water's edge.
rings: add as many more rings as you like, outward from top_bank. Each one needs a reach.
